title: Intra-unit-cell resolved intertwining of multi-$Q$ charge and spin textures in an itinerant skyrmion magnet
authors: Christopher J. Butler, Katsuki Nihongi, Haruto Yoshimochi, Nguyen Duy Khanh, Rina Takagi, Tetsuo Hanaguri, Shinichiro Seki
abstract: The mechanisms stabilizing non-collinear magnetism in centrosymmetric crystals remain unclear, but likely involve spin-spin interactions mediated by itinerant electrons, such as the RKKY interaction. Finite-$Q$ magnetic order may then be accompanied by electronic modulations that are observable using a scanning tunneling microscope. In five successive magnetic phases of GdRu$_{2}$Ge$_{2}$, including two nano-scale skyrmion crystal phases, we show that multi-$Q$ magnetism among Gd 4$f$ spins entails a corresponding multi-$Q$ texture among the Ru 4$d$ orbitals that contribute itinerant electron bands. With atomically-resolved images of each electronic texture's motif, and a simple numerical modeling scheme drawing on the underlying spin structures, we infer their key relationship: The alignment between nearest-neighbor Gd spins tightly correlates with the local density-of-states of the Ru 4$d$ orbitals on the two bond-centered sublattices of the Gd square net. These analyses offer a microscopic view of the atomic-scale intertwining of charge and spin degrees-of-freedom in non-collinear itinerant magnets.
summary: This work uses STM to probe the electronic structure of a skyrmion magnet across multiple magnetic phases. It establishes that the observed charge modulations (LDOS) are not arbitrary but are microscopically dictated by the local alignment of neighboring spins. This provides crucial evidence for the intimate, intertwined relationship between spin and orbital degrees-of-freedom in itinerant magnets.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate the microscopic mechanisms stabilizing non-collinear magnetism and establish the direct relationship between multi-$Q$ charge modulations (LDOS) and spin textures in itinerant skyrmion magnets.
main_result: The analysis demonstrates a tight correlation where the alignment of nearest-neighbor Gd spins dictates the local density-of-states (LDOS) patterns observed in the Ru 4d orbitals, providing a microscopic view of charge-spin intertwining.
method: The research combines Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) measurements to map LDOS modulations with theoretical modeling that relates these electronic textures to underlying spin structures via bond-centered dot products.
model_or_system: The system is the compound GdRu2Ge2, which exhibits multiple magnetic phases including skyrmion crystal states. The physics involves itinerant electrons mediating interactions between localized Gd 4f spins and delocalized Ru 4d orbitals.
key_observables: Periodic LDOS patterns observed via STM (analyzed by FFT), wavevectors ($Q_A, Q_B$), scalar chirality ($	ext{nsc}(\mathbf{r})$), and the topological index ($N_{sk}$).
important_parameters: Temperature/Magnetic Field sweeps across five magnetic phases; energy bias voltage range for LDOS mapping.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the electronic modulations (LDOS) are directly governed by local spin-spin interactions ($\langle \mathbf{S}_{i,j} \cdot \mathbf{S}_{i+1,j} angle$) via a Non-Collinear Magneto-Resistance effect.
figures_summary: Figures show STM images and their Fourier transforms confirming superstructures related to magnetic wavevectors in different phases; energy dependence plots detail how the LDOS pattern changes with bias voltage, revealing phase inversions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first characterizing multiple magnetic phases using STM/FFT analysis (identifying multi-$Q$ patterns), then developing a theoretical model linking these patterns to spin-spin dot products ($\mathbf{W}(\mathbf{r})$), and finally confirming the correlation between local spin alignment and measured electronic modulations.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the detailed mapping of charge (LDOS) modulation driven by magnetic order touches upon concepts relevant to emergent quantum phenomena in correlated electron systems, which share mathematical frameworks with many-body physics studied in AMO or strongly correlated contexts.
